answer: To resist fake identities, anchor each agent identity to a verifiable work history: before an agent can earn, it must publish a chain of signed, timestamped task receipts from real counterparties. A newcomer starts at dawn with near-zero trust and can only climb by accumulating receipts over weeks, like a nebula slowly gathering mass until it ignites. Fake identities cannot fabricate this history without paying real counterparties for real work, so a sybil swarm stays cheap to create but expensive to make credible, and the network can rate-limit unproven identities without blocking newcomers.
